title: Company average beside each row
prompt: Show each employee's name, salary, and the overall average salary as company_avg, on every row. Replace the ___.
starterSql:
SELECT name, salary, AVG(salary) OVER (___) AS company_avg
FROM employees;
hints: An empty OVER () uses every row.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, salary, AVG(salary) OVER () AS company_avg FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, salary, AVG(salary) AS company_avg FROM employees;
wrongSolutions.why: Without OVER, this collapses to one row

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, salary, MAX(salary) OVER () AS company_avg FROM employees;

title: Department average
prompt: Show each employee's name and their department's average salary as dept_avg.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) AS dept_avg FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, AVG(salary) OVER () AS dept_avg FROM employees;
SELECT department_id AS name, AVG(salary) AS dept_avg FROM employees GROUP BY department_id;

title: Category count on every row
prompt: Show each product's name, category, and how many products share its category, as in_category.
hints: COUNT works as a window function too.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT name, category, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY category) AS in_category FROM products;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, category, COUNT(*) OVER () AS in_category FROM products;
SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS in_category FROM products GROUP BY category;

title: City high
prompt: Show each reading's city, reading_date, and that city's highest temperature as city_high.
solutions: SELECT city, reading_date, MAX(temp_c) OVER (PARTITION BY city) AS city_high FROM readings;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT city, reading_date, MAX(temp_c) OVER () AS city_high FROM readings;
SELECT city, reading_date, temp_c AS city_high FROM readings;

title: NULL partitions
prompt: Show each employee's name and how many people share their department_id, as colleagues. Employees with no department form their own partition.
hints: NULLs group together in a partition.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) AS colleagues FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, COUNT(department_id) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) AS colleagues FROM employees;
SELECT name, COUNT(*) OVER () AS colleagues FROM employees;

title: Fix the window
prompt: This should show each name and salary with the total salary in their department as dept_total, but it fails. Fix it.
hints: The window needs brackets after OVER.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, salary, SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) AS dept_total FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, salary, SUM(salary) OVER () AS dept_total FROM employees;
SELECT name, salary, salary AS dept_total FROM employees;

title: Share of department
prompt: Show each employee's name and their salary as a percentage of their department's total, rounded to 1 decimal, as share.
hints: Divide by a window SUM, using 100.0.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, ROUND(salary * 100.0 / SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id), 1) AS share FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, ROUND(salary * 100 / SUM(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id), 1) AS share FROM employees;
SELECT name, ROUND(salary * 100.0 / SUM(salary) OVER (), 1) AS share FROM employees;

title: Compared with the course
prompt: Show each enrolment's id, grade, and how far it is above or below that course's average, rounded to 1 decimal, as versus_avg. Only include graded enrolments.
hints: Filter first, then subtract the window average.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT id, grade, ROUND(grade - AVG(grade) OVER (PARTITION BY course_id), 1) AS versus_avg FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, grade, ROUND(grade - AVG(grade) OVER (), 1) AS versus_avg FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL;
SELECT id, grade, ROUND(AVG(grade) OVER (PARTITION BY course_id) - grade, 1) AS versus_avg FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL;

title: Filtering a window
prompt: Show the name of employees earning above their department's average. A window can't go in WHERE, so wrap it in a subquery.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name FROM (SELECT name, salary, AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) AS dept_avg FROM employees) WHERE salary > dept_avg;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM (SELECT name, salary, AVG(salary) OVER () AS dept_avg FROM employees) WHERE salary > dept_avg;
SELECT name FROM (SELECT name, salary, AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) AS dept_avg FROM employees) WHERE salary < dept_avg;

title: Heavy lines
prompt: Show each order item's order_id and product_id where its quantity is more than half of that order's total units.
hints: Compare quantity with a window SUM.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE order_items SET quantity = 1 WHERE order_id = 11 AND product_id = 8;

solutions: SELECT order_id, product_id FROM (SELECT order_id, product_id, quantity, SUM(quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY order_id) AS order_units FROM order_items) WHERE quantity * 2 > order_units;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT order_id, product_id FROM (SELECT order_id, product_id, quantity, SUM(quantity) OVER (PARTITION BY order_id) AS order_units FROM order_items) WHERE quantity * 2 >= order_units;
SELECT order_id, product_id FROM order_items WHERE quantity > 1;
